coverage_claim: WM-FLW-010 covers a governed Route / Itinerary aggregate family with a mandatory kind discriminator, ordered path or itinerary composition, constraints, objectives, alternatives, selection, planned clocks, external operational bindings, validation, successor planning, estimates, provenance, access and loss-aware projections. Mode, jurisdiction, aggregate-split, routing-algorithm, implementation-conformance and independent-review questions remain deferred.

boundary_decision.rationale: Catalogue convenience justifies one aggregate family only when every instance declares route, itinerary or combined-plan. Journey execution, networks, places, schedules, resources, engines and evidence remain external masters, and a future major version may split Route and Itinerary.

decisions.rationale: Route is a reusable or computed directed path; itinerary is an ordered planning result. The aggregate is valid only with an explicit discriminator and separable identities.
Journey owns intended or actual movement and observations; Route / Itinerary owns path and plan structure, alternatives and successor history.
A reusable route may outlive computations, while a computed route is qualified by request, source dataset, engine, algorithm and parameters.
An itinerary may combine multiple routes, modes, off-network legs, activities and handover points without becoming the journey itself.
The plan records ordered references and optional geometry snapshots, while authoritative topology, places, restrictions and geometry remain external.
Requested, applied, violated or waived constraints and candidate ranking or selection rationale must not collapse into one outcome.
Requested, planned, estimated, predicted and committed clocks require independent source, authority, operating-day and timezone semantics.
The model records request, versions, parameters and results but does not own optimization implementation or execution lifecycle.

decisions.concept: OGC API Routes and Route Exchange Model
decisions.rationale: OGC material is useful for route exchange but remains developing or proposed as of 2026-09-06 and must not be presented as approved conformance.
Their route, line, journey-pattern, trip, stop-time and shape terms differ and require exact versioned mappings.
Actual temporal geometry belongs to Journey or Moving Feature evidence and may be compared with a route or itinerary without rewriting the plan.

decisions.concept: Single-provider waiver and local no-tools audit
decisions.rationale: One bounded Claude Sonnet and one bounded Grok attempt each timed out after 120 seconds. Codex separately audited the frozen validated result and comparison without acquiring new facts, so assurance remains reviewable-draft.

publication_holds: Absence-of-external-review hold: one Claude Sonnet and one Grok attempt for WM-FLW-010 each timed out after 120 seconds; no external result was admitted.
Aggregate hold: every instance must declare route, itinerary or combined-plan, and a future major version may split the aggregate into linked models.
Boundary hold: journey execution, networks, places, schedules, services, people, vehicles, bookings, activities, shipments, incidents, routing engines, source datasets and evidence remain external.
Terminology hold: route, line, journey pattern, trip, itinerary, segment, leg, waypoint, stop, call and visit have profile-specific meanings.
Standards-status hold: OGC API Routes and Route Exchange Model are developing or proposed material as of 2026-09-06, not approved OGC standards.
Mode hold: pedestrian, bicycle, road, rail, maritime, aviation, indoor, private, public, shared, freight and autonomous-route profiles need independent validation.
Jurisdiction hold: safety, accessibility, traffic, border, passenger-rights, privacy, licensing and retention rules depend on region and operating context.
Computation hold: routing and optimization algorithms, traffic prediction, feasibility solvers and benchmarks remain external implementation concerns.
Feasibility hold: a computed or selected plan does not prove resource availability, reservation, legal permission, safety or successful execution.
Privacy hold: personal itineraries and precise locations need purpose limitation, minimization, consent or other authority, protected access and deletion profiles.

Interoperability hold: every Transmodel, NeTEx, GTFS, OGC, ISO, EU, Schema.org, GeoSPARQL, GeoJSON, OWL-Time, PROV, DQV and ODRL projection needs exact release pins, conformance evidence and semantic-loss declarations.
Review hold: transport planning, geospatial, accessibility, safety, privacy, optimization, data governance, records and independent external review are outstanding.
deferred_research: Decide whether Route and Itinerary should split into separate registry models after paired implementation and query-pattern review.
Create independently validated pedestrian, bicycle, road, rail, maritime, aviation, indoor, multimodal, freight, evacuation and autonomous-route profiles.
Benchmark path continuity, transfer feasibility, map matching, traffic prediction, routing algorithms, multi-objective ranking, replanning and actual-plan divergence.

Pin exact external releases and licensing conditions and obtain independent transport, geospatial, accessibility, safety, privacy, optimization, data and records review before promotion beyond reviewable-draft assurance.
